title: Zebrafish Light/Dark Preference Test
author: Caio Maximino
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.srfed3n

steps.title: Prepare the Acrylic Tank
steps.instruction: Set up an acrylic tank (15 cm height × 10 cm width × 45 cm length) divided equally into one-half black and one-half white, including walls and bottom. Use non-reflective colored materials.

substeps.instruction: Fill the tank with de-chlorinated water to a column of 10 cm (final volume 4.5 liters).
Ensure central sliding doors are installed, colored to match the aquarium sides, defining a central compartment measuring 15 cm × 10 cm × 10 cm.

steps.title: Configure Room Environment
steps.instruction: Prepare the behavioral test room to minimize external variables.

substeps.instruction: Measure light levels to ensure they are within 2 SDs of the average, ideally between 500-600 lux above the tank.
Activate Gaussian white noise throughout the experiment to cover unwarranted room noise.

steps.title: Administer Drug or Vehicle
steps.instruction: Inject the drug or vehicle into the animal using a 10 μL microsyringe and a wetted sponge.

substeps.instruction: Anesthetize the animal using cold water (~12 ºC) or eugenol (60 ppm).
Apply an injection volume proportional to body weight (1 μL / 0.1 g).

steps.title: Acclimate Animal to Tank
steps.instruction: Introduce the animal to the testing apparatus.

substeps.instruction: Bring the animal into the behavioral test room in a temporary transport recipient.
Use a net to transfer the animal to the central compartment of the tank.
Allow the animal to acclimate for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Conduct Light/Dark Preference Test
steps.instruction: Observe the animal's behavior as it explores the different compartments.

substeps.instruction: Remove the sliding doors to allow the fish to swim freely for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Remove Animal from Tank
steps.instruction: Transfer the animal to a discard tank using a net.

steps.title: Analyze Behavioral Data
steps.instruction: Analyze videos blindly using two experienced researchers and an event/spatial distribution logger (e.g., X-Plo-Rat 1.1.0 Windows).

substeps.instruction: Record time spent, latency to enter, number of entries, and duration of entries in the white compartment.
Record 'Risk assessment' events (fast <1 s entry into white compartment followed by re-entry into black, or partial entry where pectoral fin does not cross midline).
Record duration and number of erratic swimming (zig-zag, fast, unpredictable course) and freezing events (cessation of movement except eye and opercular movements).
Record time on thigmotaxis (swimming within 2 cm or less from the nearest wall).

If using X-Plo-Rat, assign risk assessment, erratic swimming, freezing, and thigmotaxis to keyboard keys (e.g., A, S, D, and F) and use the I-maze pre-configuration with 'walled' squares as the black compartment.
